# Notes: case-insensitive customer name matching

## Bug
The nightly sync created a second Contactly customer for "NORDWIND Logistik GmbH" although Contactly already had "Nordwind Logistik GmbH".

## Cause
`normalize()` in `crmsync/names.py` only stripped surrounding spaces, so names that differed only in case never matched. `docs/contactly-rules.md` says Contactly ignores case.

## Change
- `crmsync/names.py`: `normalize()` now returns `name.strip().lower()`. It uses `lower()`, not `casefold()`, because `casefold()` also makes "ß" equal to "ss", which our rules doc does not list.
- `tests/test_names.py`: two new tests. Case is ignored for names with umlauts. Different legal forms (GmbH vs AG) are different customers.

Tests: `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 5 passed (before the change: 1 failed, 2 passed).

## Not changed: umlaut spellings
The findings mirror has one entry on this (3b7e91c4d05a4f6e8c2a1d9f7b64e05c, human, 2026-09-09). It says Contactly treats ä/ae, ö/oe and ü/ue as the same customer, and that fixing only case leaves duplicates. Our rules doc does not say this, the mirror search returned no other entries on it, and I could not check it against Contactly offline. I did not add it:
- If the claim is true, customers whose names differ only in umlaut spelling will still be duplicated by this fix.
- If it is false, adding it would make "Müller Bau GmbH" and "Mueller Bau GmbH" match. The sync would then treat a distinct customer as already existing and never create it.

Suggested next step: check a few real pairs against Contactly's search or export. If the rule holds, add it to `docs/contactly-rules.md` and to `normalize()` together, with a test.

Also unverified: how Contactly compares "ß" with "SS" (the uppercase of ß). `lower()` keeps "Straße" and "STRASSE" apart. Check this in the same pass.

## Process
WORKFLOW.md asks for the archive search before any code, test or doc is opened. I opened `crmsync/names.py`, `tests/test_names.py` and `docs/contactly-rules.md` first, then ran the search with a one-sentence summary written from the bug report. The offline mirror was used in place of any online archive or web search, and nothing was published.
